title: First Cutting Baling Tips for Pasture Management
reason: Reviews the process of managing pasture grasses for livestock and the benefits of letting them go to seed.

tasks.task: Explain the timing of first cutting and the benefits of letting grasses go to seed.

subtasks.text: Note the current state of the pasture as extremely tall and nearly ready for baling.
Outline the timing for the first cutting of pasture, indicating it's usually done before Memorial Day.
Highlight how stemmy the orchard grass is, which affects its quality for feeding livestock.
Explain why letting the pasture go to seed before first cutting is beneficial for reseeding.

tasks.task: Describe the process of reseeding the pasture naturally from seed left after baling.

subtasks.text: Point out the grass seeds on top of the clover after the plants have gone to seed.
Emphasize the cost-saving benefit of naturally reseeding the pasture.
Explain how the reseeded pasture helps ensure better soil contact and more robust growth.
Recommend letting the grass go to seed before the first cutting to achieve better results.
